itemized_evaluation.justification: The paper includes an explicit funding source disclosure and conflict of interest statement in 'Notes on the record': 'Funding: none received; independent research.' and 'Competing interests: D.S. is the founder and a beneficiary of FreshCredit Inc. and the founder of The FreshCredit Lab. FreshCredit Inc holds granted US utility patents...'

The text explicitly refers to its companion works as preprints (e.g., 'companion theory preprint') and contains no explicit journal name, peer-review credentials, or institutional repository publication statement for the manuscript itself.

Prior works are accurately represented with extreme rigor against misquoting or selective framing. In Section 1.1: '(A widely circulated claim that “95% of synthetic identities pass onboarding undetected,” attributed to Thomson Reuters across vendor blogs, has no locatable primary source, methodology, or date; we treat it as an unverifiable industry statistic and do not rely on it.)' Also in Section 1.1: 'Experimental demand characteristics show heterogeneous, bidirectional participation effects with frequent nulls — 12 of 19 studies positive, 5 clear nulls; the review concludes little is securely known about conditions, mechanisms, or magnitudes.'

The paper establishes a fully reproducible protocol and references independent confirmations. In 'Notes on the record': 'All simulation code, seeds, formal SMT proofs, high-resolution figures, and pre-registration documents are permanently deposited and publicly accessible in the open research archive (Release v4.3, https://github.com/devonshigaki/trust-stack-research-collection/releases/tag/v4.3) with cryptographic SHA-256 manifest verification... Every mathematical invariant and empirical claim is verified via an automated 26-task continuous integration test harness executing with 100% zero-failure reproducibility.' In Section 3.4: 'independently corroborated by on Base'.

Sampling and initialization in simulations are explicitly randomized and controlled for systematic measurement bias. In Section 3.6: 'The full-circle stereographic map gives R = 0.040 ± 0.021 at K = 0, at the finite-size floor 1/sqrt(500) ≈ 0.045; raw uniform phases give 0.039 ± 0.020' and in Section 3.7: 'Directed information flow between a fixed agent and a validator, measured by surrogate-corrected transfer entropy... The pre-registered hypothesis — bilateral validation is symmetric, surveillance is not — survives a bias-corrected estimator; the uncorrected estimator inverts the result'.

Sample sizes and resolution limits are explicitly justified and analyzed for natural variability/seed noise. In Section 1.4: 'a 9-seed fine scan at K = 4.5 gives R ≈ 0.69–0.74 across l in [0, 0.10], first below-0.7 reading at l = 0.08; the exact crossing is not resolvable at seed noise ± 0.02–0.03... (ranges span two independent seeded re-renders; point precision is not resolvable at these N).' In Section 3.3: 'a target hypothesis whose corridor half-width is a pre-registered smallest effect size of interest (SESOI)'.

The simulation designs use proper controls (isolated K=0, raw uniform phases, surrogate-corrected controls, zero-knowledge controls) and pre-frozen criteria that prevent post-hoc experimenter bias (the simulation equivalent of blinding). In Section 3.6: 'versus the isolated control (K = 0) across 8 replicas... and the phase-map-control side panel'. In Section 4: 'pre-registered with frozen pass/fail criteria before any data contact... C2, a zero-knowledge-observation control with |bias| <= 0.01'.

Correct statistical tests (non-parametric permutation tests, sign-flip tests, surrogate-corrected transfer entropy) are applied and effect sizes are explicitly reported alongside p-values. In Section 3.6 (Sim P4b): 'energy distance 0.00021, permutation p = 0.005 (2,000 permutations) against the pre-registered p < 0.05... What the result actually shows is narrower than the old headline... an energy distance of 0.00021 is practically negligible at the tested scale'. In Section 3.7 (Sim P7): 'a mean paired reduction of 0.441, permutation p = 0.004 (2,000 sign-flips, 8 replicas).'

Method of randomization (exact random seeds, distributions) and group/agent allocations are fully detailed. In Section 3.6: 'N = 500 agents; per-event validation settlement on x402-class rails; per-tenant trust records; 20% adversarial event rate... ω ~ Cauchy(0,1); stereographic initialization; dt = 0.05... seed 42.' In Section 3.7: 'A population of present-biased agents (β ~ U(0.4, 0.9), δ ~ U(0.95, 0.999), horizons 6–24 steps)' and '10% mutant subpopulation'.

Standard deviations, 95% confidence intervals, and exact p-values are clearly reported throughout. In Section 3.2: '95% CI [-44.2, -43.2]; R^2 = 0.984'. In Section 3.6: 'R = 0.739 ± 0.029 coupled vs. 0.040 ± 0.001 isolated', 'permutation p = 0.005', 'p = 0.109'. In Section 3.7: 'agent->validator 0.0315 ± 0.003 bits, validator->agent 0.0283 ± 0.002 bits — 95% CIs across 8 replicas', 'permutation p = 0.004'.

Raw numbers, baseline numbers, and absolute risks are explicitly provided alongside relative percentages. In Section 3.6 (Sim P2): 'compromises 100% of records; a breach under database-per-tenant isolation compromises exactly the breached tenants (0.2% at N = 500) — a 99.8% relative reduction in conditional exposure'. In Section 3.9: 'N_all = 3 x 10^8 records in the centralized reference... Centralized expected exposure at p_org = 0.05: 15M records/yr (6M at 0.02; 30M at 0.10). Per-tenant wins ~8x in the favorable region — p_device = 0.005, p_commonmode = 0.001 -> E_T = 1.8M vs. 15M — and loses when endpoint multiplication dominates: p_device = 0.06 -> E_T = 18.3M > 15M'.

Failed runs, null results, and data exclusions are fully logged and accounted for. In Section 3.2: 'A -31.6%/year fit on a small subsample (df = 7) is unreconstructable from the cited series... and is not used'. In Section 3.7: 'The stack’s rule applies here unchanged: nulls and failed estimators stay in the record next to the successes.' In Section 4: 'The first-run estimator defect (an ad-hoc estimator producing symmetric garbage) was caught by the frozen criteria, archived, and disclosed with the run record.'

The paper strictly maintains outcome metric consistency and explicitly refuses to conflate simulation or component metrics with end-to-end or clinical/domain claims. In Section 1.1: 'A scope boundary is stated up front: vulnerability-free verifiable events (credential checks, device attestations) yield a verification/reputation state, not trust dynamics in the theory’s sense'. In Section 1.5: 'No achieved end-to-end performance is claimed for deployed applications of the protocol.' In Section 3.6: 'The defensible comparison is marginal-vs-marginal... A “$50 per record pull” anchor... is not commensurate with the protocol’s marginal settlement fee, and no headline reduction derived from it (e.g., “99.998% below baseline”) is claimed.'

Statistical significance is explicitly distinguished from practical impact. In Section 3.6 (Sim P4b): 'the terminal trust-vector distribution of the heterogeneous population is statistically distinguishable from the homogeneous reference: energy distance 0.00021, permutation p = 0.005 (2,000 permutations) against the pre-registered p < 0.05... What the result actually shows is narrower than the old headline: the seeding variable is not inert... but an energy distance of 0.00021 is practically negligible at the tested scale, so “heterogeneity matters for terminal outcomes” is supported only in the statistical sense, not in the effect-size sense'.

Confirmatory vs. definitional mechanisms and confounding variables (such as demand characteristics, Campbell's law, and memecoin volume inflation) are explicitly controlled for and discussed. In Section 3.4: 'headline x402 volume figures are inflated by late-2025 memecoin activity — the PING mint spike and retry/test traffic — but the claim here rests on demonstrated sub-cent settlement cost'. In Section 3.6: 'component (i) of the leakage operationalization (K_eff = K(1-l)) makes part of the R-decay definitional... The identification of expropriative observation with channel attenuation is a modeling assumption, not a derivation'. In Section 4: 'Campbell’s law applies to the protocol’s own metrics.'

Figures and charts are described with full baseline and axis transparency, including explicit detection floors, finite-size floors, and error bars. In Figure 4 caption: 'isolated R = 0.040 ± 0.001, at the 1/sqrt(N) ≈ 0.045 finite-size floor'. In Figure 10 caption: '95% CIs across 8 replicas, with the 0.01-bit detection floor marked... Magnitudes are floor-adjacent, so no ratio headline is reported.' In Figure 5 caption: 'Phase arrows are seeded schematic draws; only the printed re-run values are measured.'

Hypotheses and criteria were pre-specified and registered prior to data collection, with explicit refusal to adjust thresholds post-hoc. In Section 1.4: 'The hypothesis below matches the tested design (§3.6) and is the registered form (specified and timestamped in the Supporting Document; an OSF registration of the same design filed with the deposit (Release v4.3, Accession: https://github.com/devonshigaki/trust-stack-research-collection/releases/tag/v4.3) prior to any pilot data collection).' In Section 4: 'An instrument-recalibration pass (regression-initialized EM) did not move any criterion across its frozen threshold, and no threshold was adjusted post hoc. The verdict is reported as FAIL'.

Study durations and long-run temporal validity are explicitly modeled over multi-year horizons to detect cold-start traps, stalls, and relapses. In Section 3.10: 'All of the stack’s dynamics evidence is short-horizon; this section reports the long-run and cold-start analyses... The leak-free symmetric limit (theory preset) accumulates unbounded values under a stationary honest stream (S = 249 after 10^5 events)... escape times run 318 ± 133 days at r_floor = 0.01/day... Outcomes are classified as compound (<= 10 yr to 50% adoption), stall, or reversal'.

Regression models, throughput figures, and trends are explicitly bounded against improper extrapolation. In Section 3.2: 'the trend is era-split (Figure 3): a re-fit on the full sourced Komorowski table (273 transcribed drive-price points, 1980–2009) gives a log-linear decline of -43.7%/year... while the modern era is much flatter — fleet endpoints give ≈ -14%/year over 2009–2022... with the caveat that the 2025–26 NAND shortage reversed SSD pricing (enterprise +257%) while HDDs continued the trend (+35%) — a 46-year pattern, not a law'. In Section 3.4: 'the often-quoted 623,230 TPS figure is Parity’s linear extrapolation to 100 cores, not a measurement'.

Results adhere strictly to mathematical boundaries and domain reality. In Section 3.3: 'where the trust index ι(T) = tanh(w T_tilde) in (-1, 1) distorts outcome probabilities by a bounded exponential tilt... At neutral trust (ι = 0) this is exactly standard expected utility; the distortion is bounded (|log P_tilde/P| <= 2γ max|u_hat|...), so trust reweights evidence but never manufactures outcomes.' In Section 3.7: 'P5b’s initial increment measure — |Σ ΔT| — is identically zero on the simplex, so its first kurtosis value was a property of float rounding error. Both artifacts and their corrections are documented in §Q.'
